en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourteenth Chapter
The Discussion on the Latent Disposition Being Different:
Is the latent disposition of sensual lust one thing and the obsession of sensual lust another? Yes.
Is sensual lust one thing and the obsession by sensual lust another?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is that very same sensual lust the obsession by sensual lust?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is that very underlying tendency to sensual lust the same as the obsession by sensual lust?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … .
Is the underlying tendency to aversion one thing and the obsession by aversion another?
Yes. Is aversion one thing and the obsession by aversion another? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is that very same aversion the obsession by aversion? Yes.
Is that very underlying tendency to aversion the same as the obsession by aversion?
One should not say so… [and so on] … Is the underlying tendency to conceit one thing and the obsession by conceit another?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is conceit one thing and the obsession by conceit another?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is that very conceit itself the obsession by conceit? Yes.
Is that very underlying tendency to conceit itself the obsession by conceit? [No.]
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to views one thing and the obsession by views another? Yes.
Is view one thing and the obsession by view another?
One should not say so …pe… Is that very same view the obsession by view?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is that very latent tendency of views (diṭṭhānusaya) the same as the obsession of views (diṭṭhipariyuṭṭhāna)?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is the underlying tendency to doubt one thing and the obsession by doubt another?
Yes. Is doubt one thing and the obsession by doubt another? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is that very doubt the obsession by doubt? Yes.
Is that very underlying tendency of doubt the same as the obsession of doubt?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency of lust for existence one thing and the obsession of lust for existence another? One should not say so.
“Yes,” you say.
“Is craving for existence one thing and the obsession by craving for existence another?
You must not say so … [and so on] …
Is that very craving for existence itself the obsession by craving for existence?
Yes. Is that very underlying tendency to craving for existence itself the obsession by craving for existence? Yes.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is the underlying tendency to ignorance one thing and the obsession by ignorance another? Yes.
Is ignorance one thing and the obsession by ignorance another?
One should not say so …pe… Is that very same ignorance the obsession by ignorance?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that very underlying tendency to ignorance (avijjānusaya) the same as the obsession by ignorance (avijjāpariyuṭṭhāna)?
You should not speak thus … [as before] … .
Is it not to be said that the underlying tendency is one thing and the obsession is another?
Yes, it is.
Is it to be said that an ordinary person (puthujjana), while a wholesome or indeterminate consciousness is occurring, is "possessed of latent tendencies" (sānusaya)?
Yes. Is it to be said that he is "obsessed" (pariyuṭṭhita)? No.
It should not be said so.
For if that were the case, then the underlying tendency (anusaya) would be one thing and the active obsession (pariyuṭṭhāna) another.
Furthermore, when a wholesome or indeterminate state of consciousness is occurring, should an ordinary person (puthujjana) be called "one possessed of lust" (sarāga)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then one should be called ‘obsessed’?
“One should not be so called.”
In that case, lust is one thing and obsession is another.
The discussion on whether the underlying tendency is distinct [from these] is concluded.
